utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: What about his relationship with his wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a wonderful relationship as husband and wife. They were truly in love.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did Dusko love children, especially his own children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Valentina in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Excuse me just one moment. (Pause.) Witness, by the agreement of counsel, the Trial Chamber will refer to you as witness BB. We do not want your name to be made a matter of public record, but Mr. Vujin is writing what he considers to be your name on a piece of paper. It will be shown to the Prosecutor, and then it will be shown to you and then you will have to confirm that that is your name. So if you will just wait a few moments, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You have no additional questions, Mr. Vujin? And you have no questions, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Then that is it. Thank you very much for coming. You are free to leave now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Vujin, your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Valentina Tadic. Valentina Tadic (sworn).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Miss Tadic. You may be seated. Mr. Vujin, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Miss Valentina, you are the daughter of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: I know that it's very difficult for you at this moment, but I kindly ask you and we're not going to question you for long. We just want to put a few questions to you to the extent to which you can answer about your relationship with your father and perhaps a few words about your family. How old are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: 17. Do you have vivid memories of your father while you were together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I remember that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: So let us break your stage fright. I want to show you a picture done by your father. Do you recognise yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: So we submit this to the Chamber as evidence. This will be for you. (Handed) Do you know about the fact that your father painted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did he do that often? Did he like doing that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he always liked doing that. He always liked to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: This was by way of introduction and also to break your stage fright. Miss Valentina, can you remember that far back, when you were a young girl, a little girl? Can you tell us about the relationship between your father and your mother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The relationship between my mother and father were good. They loved each other. They always agreed on everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did they quarrel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they never quarrelled. Perhaps -- I was an only child and my father paid a lot of attention to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: When was your sister born later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nine years later. For nine years I was an only child.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: During those years were you the apple of your father's eye?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: How did your father express his love for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would always walk together. He would take me to the cinema. I also trained karate with him, since I was a very young girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: So you trained karate. How many of you trained karate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Were there a lot of boys and girls who trained karate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did you have good friends, boys and girls amongst them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Most of my friends trained karate with me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Who was your best friend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sinita Siviz was my best friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Sinita Siviz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: What was she by ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A Muslim, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Where did she live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was my neighbour. She lived nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: You played together. You were inseparable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we also went to school together, to the same class.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Let's go back to your father. Was he strict or was he lenient?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was never strict.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: When you would do something wrong as a child, who was the person who would talk to you, perhaps punish you? It was your father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. My mother most occasions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did your father play with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: What were the situations like and how often was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, often, whenever he would have enough time. He paid a lot of attention to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did you also play with boys and girls, your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, with all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: What were the games involved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The games ... we would ride bicycles. We would play different ball games.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Who taught you how to ride a bicycle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My friends. Together we would ride a bicycle.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did your father teach you how to ride a bicycle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. I never saw my father ride a bicycle. I don't think he knows how to ride a bicycle.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: You think he doesn't know how to ride a bicycle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: How old were you when mummy went to Libya?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How old? I think I was six.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember that period? Who took care of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember very well. Daddy and I lived together and he took care of me and mummy went there to earn a living and to make enough money for our future life.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did you know whether mummy and daddy tried to go abroad elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I remember. They always wanted to go abroad, Australia, Canada.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Why didn't they actually do this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure. The South African Republic, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: While your father took care of you, while he was with you, were there any problems in terms of preparing the food, your clothing, etc?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. He would prepare breakfast and lunch and whatever was needed, everything I needed, and we agreed with each other invariably.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Do you love your father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Do you think he loves you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Does he love your mother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Your younger sister?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He loves her but I think that I'm his pet.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Could you say something else about your father, what he was like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I could say that --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Was he gentle? Was he strict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was always gentle towards me. I always had whatever I wished for and my great wish was to have a motorbike, and he said that he would never buy a motorbike for me because it was dangerous.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did he drive a motorbike?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did you ever see your father drunk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drunk? No. No. He would never drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: He led the life of a sportsman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was always the sports type, and he raised me in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: In a sports spirit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in a sports spirit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did he tell you about the values a person should have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: What did he tell you? What was the most valuable thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he would always tell me that I should be involved in sports, that I should lead a healthy life.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Did he raise you to become a good person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: To be a sincere person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and to work with others.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have no questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Miss Tadic, thank you very much for coming. You are excused. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Vujin, would you call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness would be Mira Tadic, but her questioning would probably take a bit longer. At this point in time the defence is not prepared to start with that, so I kindly request that we continue with that tomorrow and we start questioning her tomorrow, bearing in mind our obligation with the psychologist so that we had to look into.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Do you have another witness to call instead of Mira Tadic at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: No. Mr. Petrovic was not brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: The Registry advises that Mr. Petrovic was not there at the hotel. That's why they were not able to bring him over.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. Yes, I am familiar with that. Since it's 5 o'clock, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: We had planned on proceeding until 5.30 every day this week, except for Friday, if we have not completed. We will begin at 2.30 and adjourn at 5.00 pm. The reason is we have to expeditiously use our time in the courtroom. You can speak with the Registry representative about the report from the psychologist who examined Mr. Tadic and if the report is to be submitted, it would be requested that you provide it to the Trial Chamber this evening, if you can, and if there's nothing else, then we will adjourn until -- yes, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: There was that matter I raised earlier, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. In closed session. Let's resolve it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I don't think it has to be closed. I think they just turn off the outside --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: That is true. We decided we would do that. We will just turn off the microphones going outside.
